title: Publish to a stable listener snapshot
prompt: Complete Signal::publish. Call subscribers in registration order. Subscribers added during a publication must start receiving events only on the next publication. No unsubscribe or concurrent access is required.
signature: class Signal: void subscribe(std::function<void(int)>); void publish(int)

tests.label: Registration order
tests.hint: Visit the snapshot in its stored order.

tests.label: Value delivered
tests.hint: Pass the published value to the listener.

tests.label: New listener waits
tests.hint: Iterate over a snapshot, not the vector being changed.

tests.label: No listeners
tests.hint: An empty subscriber list is valid.

hints: Adding to the original vector while iterating it may invalidate iteration.
Copy the listener list before invoking callbacks.
explanation: The snapshot makes the notification boundary explicit and avoids iterator invalidation caused by new subscribers. It does not make the signal thread-safe or define recursive publication policies.
